task_metadata.research_topic: protein mutation effect prediction from frozen ESM-2 embeddings
task_metadata.research_question: Design a supervised prediction head over frozen ESM-2 embeddings and delta embeddings that improves mutation effect prediction on ProteinGym DMS assays.
notes: The task is a supervised protein fitness prediction problem over precomputed embeddings, not end-to-end sequence modeling.
The three evaluated assays are ProteinGym splits tied to Firnberg 2014, Nutschel 2020, and Bandaru 2017.

tests.label: BLAT_ECOLX
tests.notes: ProteinGym benchmark split for the beta-lactamase fitness landscape from Firnberg et al.

tests.label: ESTA_BACSU
tests.notes: ProteinGym benchmark split for Bacillus subtilis lipase/esterase thermostability from Nutschel et al.

tests.label: RASH_HUMAN
tests.notes: ProteinGym benchmark split for Ras mutational effects from Bandaru et al.

baselines.name: ridge
baselines.notes: L2-regularized linear regression head (single nn.Linear trained with AdamW, weight_decay=5e-2). Matches the supervised 'Embeddings' linear baseline used in ProteinGym/ProteinNPT, which trains a linear head on mean-pooled PLM features with weight decay rather than the closed-form sklearn estimator.

baselines.name: mlp
baselines.notes: Single-hidden-layer MLP head (Linear -> Dropout -> ReLU -> Linear) over mean-pooled ESM-2 features. Matches the canonical nonlinear probe used in TAPE / ProteinGym / ProteinNPT supervised baselines; intentionally not a deep residual MLP.

baselines.name: reshape_cnn
baselines.notes: Reshape-CNN: concatenates [mutant_emb, delta_emb] (2*1280=2560 dims), reshapes to (channels=64, length=40), and applies Conv1D blocks over the embedding-channel axis. NOT a paper-faithful per-residue CNN: the precomputed embedding files only store mean-pooled features, so there is no real residue/sequence axis. Renamed from 'cnn' to make this clear; the reference is LeCun 1998 only as a generic CNN family pointer, not as a faithful re-implementation.

papers.title: ProteinGym: Large-Scale Benchmarks for Protein Fitness Prediction and Design
papers.relevance: Defines the benchmark protocol and the supervised mutation-effect evaluation used by this task.

papers.title: ProteinNPT: Improving Protein Property Prediction and Design with Non-Parametric Transformers
papers.relevance: Provides a modern protein property prediction baseline suite that explicitly reuses ridge-style supervised heads.

papers.title: Biological structure and function emerge from scaling unsupervised learning to 250 million protein sequences

papers.title: Language models of protein sequences at the scale of evolution enable accurate structure prediction
papers.relevance: Direct source for the ESM-2 650M embeddings used by the task.

papers.title: Evaluating Protein Transfer Learning with TAPE
papers.relevance: Canonical benchmark paper for supervised and transfer learning with protein representations.

papers.title: Deep generative models of genetic variation capture the effects of mutations
papers.relevance: Foundational unsupervised mutation-effect predictor that established a strong protein-fitness baseline.

papers.title: Disease variant prediction with deep generative models of evolutionary data
papers.relevance: EVE is a major unsupervised variant-effect baseline for protein mutation scoring.

papers.title: MSA Transformer
papers.relevance: Important protein language model baseline and a representative alternative embedding family.

papers.title: FLIP: Benchmark tasks in fitness landscape inference for proteins
papers.relevance: Close benchmark analogue for protein fitness prediction under distribution shift.

papers.title: A comprehensive, high-resolution map of a gene's fitness landscape
papers.relevance: Original deep mutational scanning source for the BLAT_ECOLX assay.

papers.title: Systematically Scrutinizing the Impact of Substitution Sites on Thermostability and Detergent Tolerance for Bacillus subtilis Lipase A

papers.title: Deconstruction of the Ras switching cycle through saturation mutagenesis
papers.relevance: Original deep mutational scanning source for the RASH_HUMAN assay.

papers.title: Ridge Regression: Biased Estimation for Nonorthogonal Problems
papers.relevance: Canonical ridge regression reference for the linear baseline.

papers.title: Learning representations by back-propagating errors
papers.relevance: Classic backprop-trained multilayer perceptron reference for the nonlinear baseline.

papers.relevance: Classic CNN reference. Used here only as a generic citation for the convolutional family; the 'reshape_cnn' baseline is NOT a paper-faithful re-implementation (it convolves over the embedding-channel axis, not a residue sequence).
